text.arabic_uthmani: ثَانِىَ عِطْفِهِۦ لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ لَهُۥ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا خِزْىٌۭ ۖ وَنُذِيقُهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ عَذَابَ ٱلْحَرِيقِ

words.gloss_range: circumstantial active participle of bending or turning, continuing the prior disputer as a visible posture rather than starting a new subject
words.root_gloss_range: folding, bending, turning, doubling, and recurrence; here the local construct selects bodily turning while recurrence remains contrastive pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ثَانِىَ}} ({{tr:thāniya}}) opens as an accusative circumstantial participle, so the reader carries the disputer from 22:8 into a posture rather than meeting a new actor. Its folding and turning field makes the argument become visible in the body, especially in the unique folded-side idiom, while the active participle keeps that posture simultaneous with the following purpose clause. The recurrence contrast with the paired-repeated field (15:87; 39:23) remains a corpus pressure, not the selected local sense.

topics.headline: circumstantial posture continues the prior disputer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins mid-portrait, carrying the 22:8 disputer forward as a posture before any new verdict appears.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as an accusative circumstantial participle linked to the prior context.

topics.headline: folding root makes argument bodily
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the disputation harden into a body turned away, while broader recurrence senses remain only contrastive.
topics.reason: The local construct with the following side word licenses bodily turning; references to paired recurrence are useful contrasts (15:87; 39:23) but do not replace the local posture.

topics.headline: opening sound tightens into side word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening word move into the constricted side image instead of treating the posture as only conceptual.
topics.reason: The sound observation is tied to the immediate next word and reinforces the embodied posture without changing lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: his side or flank in a construct phrase, with possessive force and a live side-sympathy contrast from accepted variant evidence
words.root_gloss_range: side, flank, inclination, sympathy, and turning toward; here the surface selects the bodily side while variant and root pressure keep withheld inclination visible

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accepted variant pressure toward sympathy or inclination while the local surface remains his side

words.prose: {{ar:عِطْفِهِۦ}} ({{tr:ʿiṭfihi}}) supplies the body part that the participle bends, and the suffix keeps it attached to the same tracked man. The side is not a generic idiom floating free; it is his own flank turned away. Because the root also bears inclination and sympathy pressure, and variant evidence points toward {{ar:عَطْفِهِ}} ({{tr:ʿaṭfihi}}), the gesture carries an affective refusal: the body-side also suggests withheld leaning or compassion. The hapax status concentrates that body-and-empathy portrait in one rare word.

topics.headline: possessed side completes the posture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the arrogance is localized in the man’s own side rather than left as an abstract attitude.
topics.reason: The word is genitive after the participial head and carries a 3ms suffix, so it specifies the bent body part of the tracked disputer.

topics.headline: side and sympathy share pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the turned flank also as a refusal of receptive inclination, while the local surface still means his side.
topics.reason: The surface reading selects the body-side sense; accepted variant and root-family evidence preserve sympathy or inclination as pressure without replacing the local noun.

topics.headline: geminated forms intensify the posture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can register heavier posture pressure from variant form evidence without changing the local referent.
topics.reason: The geminated variants sharpen degree or habitual force but do not alter the governed body-part role.

topics.headline: hapax root compresses body and empathy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this rare root makes the posture unusually diagnostic, not a routine word for arrogance.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows treat the root as Quranically unique and combine that rarity with the accepted side-sympathy pressure.

words.root_display: no lexical root (particle or function word)
words.gloss_range: attached purpose/result particle governing the following subjunctive verb and tying posture to misguidance
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) is small, but it makes the posture move toward the following misguiding verb. It governs the verb’s subjunctive mood, so the link is grammatical before it is interpretive. Its purpose-result range lets the sentence cover intended misleading and produced deviation, and its position closes the posture beat before the verdict begins.

topics.headline: particle governs the misguiding verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that misguidance is grammatically dependent on the posture, not simply the next action in a list.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the particle as governing the following subjunctive verb in the purpose clause.

topics.headline: purpose and result remain in play
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear both culpable aim and consequential outcome without splitting the syntax into two claims.
topics.reason: The local construction is purpose-linked, while the CRITICAL rows preserve the recognized resultative pressure of the particle.

topics.headline: purpose particle closes the posture beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah finish motive before it turns to assigned punishment.
topics.reason: The purpose clause follows the posture phrase and precedes the fronted verdict clause.

words.gloss_range: causative subjunctive misguiding, projected as aim or outcome and aimed away from a named divine path rather than vague error
words.root_gloss_range: straying, losing the way, error, disappearance, and causative leading astray; local Form IV with the path complement selects causing deviation
words.prose: {{ar:يُضِلَّ}} ({{tr:yuḍilla}}) is subordinate to the preceding particle and keeps the same singular disputer as agent, so the bent posture becomes projected misguidance. Because it is followed by a path phrase, the lost-way root is locally concrete: he causes route-removal, not just generic error. The canonical Form IV exports deviation to others, while the Form I variant keeps the agent’s own straying visible as a linked possibility. The phrase also joins a wider formula (31:6) and a nearby root movement from act to verdict (22:12).

topics.headline: subjunctive verb keeps the same agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices one continuous disputer moving from posture into projected misguiding.
topics.reason: The verb is 3ms imperfect subjunctive after the particle, tied to the same prior disputer.

topics.headline: lost-way root is literalized by path complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees misguidance as removal from a course, not as a floating mental error.
topics.reason: The following prepositional path complement licenses route-deviation language for the root.

topics.headline: causative and self-straying readings interact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees outward corrupting agency in the standard form, with variant evidence preserving the agent’s own loss of direction as contrast.
topics.reason: The standard aligned surface is Form IV causative; the Form I reading is valid contrast but does not govern the local parse.

topics.headline: misguiding phrase belongs to a formulaic field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this act of misguiding within a recurring obstruction formula and then sees the same root become verdict nearby.
topics.reason: The phrase is compared with the same formula (31:6) and with the root’s later verdict form in this surah (22:12).

topics.headline: doubled sound turns toward separation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the doubled verb sound pivot into the separating preposition that follows.
topics.reason: The sound note is locally attached to the verb and the following separation marker.

words.root_display: no lexical root (particle or function word)
words.gloss_range: separation preposition governing the path phrase, selecting departure away from the path rather than topical speech about it
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) turns the misguiding into separation from a path. Although the particle can have other uses, the verb-plus-path frame selects departure, so the issue is not merely talking about God’s way or acting on its behalf. The preposition also prevents the verb from collapsing into a direct attack on the path itself; the image is diversion off the course.

topics.headline: separation from the path
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that misguidance is measured as distance from a reference path.
topics.reason: The particle governs the path noun after a misguiding verb, which selects separation over topical or substitutional readings.

topics.headline: path is not directly destroyed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees diversion from the path rather than a direct object relation where the path itself is destroyed.
topics.reason: The verb instance has a prepositional complement rather than an explicit direct object path.

words.gloss_range: singular construct path or course, governed by separation and made definite by the divine possessor
words.root_gloss_range: path, way, road, course, means, and channel; here the abstract singular construct selects a divine course departed from
words.prose: {{ar:سَبِيلِ}} ({{tr:sabīli}}) is the path from which the misguidance separates people, and as a construct head it receives definiteness and authority from the following divine name. Its overwhelmingly abstract usage keeps the path as a moral or religious course rather than a literal road, though the channel image can still make diversion feel like being pulled out of a guided flow. The singular construct narrows many possible routes into one recognized divine course, a formula that returns in the surah’s obstruction language (22:25; 22:58).

topics.headline: singular construct path of God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the path is one identified divine course, not a set of optional routes.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the separation preposition and construct-bound to the following divine name.

topics.headline: abstract path with channel pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the path as a traversable moral course, with channel imagery adding movement without making it a literal road.
topics.reason: The occurrence profile supports abstract path/course as local sense; watercourse pressure survives as image only.

topics.headline: path formula seeds surah obstruction motif
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a familiar divine-path formula that will return in local obstruction language.
topics.reason: The collocation and inter-ayah rows connect the formula with later references in the surah, especially 22:25 and 22:58.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as genitive possessor, closing the path phrase with named authority
words.root_gloss_range: divinity, worship, godhood, and the proper divine name; here the proper name anchors authority and worship rather than a generic deity class
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) closes the path phrase as the genitive possessor, so the deviation is theological before the punishment sentence begins. The proper name makes the path a named-authority relation rather than a generic method. Etymological worship and bewilderment pressure can sharpen the seriousness of leaving the path, but the local form remains the proper divine name. The placement also ties the phrase into a dense divine-authority field around this section.

topics.headline: proper name anchors the path
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the path’s authority is fixed by the divine proper name, not by an abstract principle.
topics.reason: The word is the genitive possessor in the construct path phrase and is a proper noun rather than a generic class noun.

topics.headline: worship and bewilderment pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can feel that leaving this path is not merely social misdirection, while the local word remains the proper name.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute is useful as pressure but does not replace the local proper-name reading.

topics.headline: divine name saturates the local frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the path and misguidance field measured against the named divine source across the section.
topics.reason: Contextual profiles support the divine name as a local anchor for the path and misguidance fields.

words.root_display: no lexical root (particle or function word)
words.gloss_range: fronted preposition-pronoun assigning the coming disgrace to the same tracked man
words.prose: {{ar:لَهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) shifts the ayah from description into assigned verdict. The fronted predicate names the recipient before the domain and disgrace appear, so the punishment is specifically for the same 3ms figure tracked by the earlier possessive suffix and later object suffix. Its particle also mirrors the earlier purpose particle: his purpose leads to his due.

topics.headline: fronted predicate assigns disgrace
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verdict being allocated to him before the disgrace itself is named.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the phrase as a fronted predicate paired with the delayed disgrace noun.

topics.headline: purpose particle answered by due particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the earlier purpose marker answered by a verdict marker, turning aim into assigned consequence.
topics.reason: The repeated particle form links the purpose clause to the punishment allocation without making the two particles identical in function.

words.root_display: no lexical root (particle or function word)
words.gloss_range: locative-domain preposition placing the disgrace within the nearer life
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) makes the nearer life the domain that contains the disgrace. Whether it is read as framing the disgrace noun directly or the whole allocation clause, the effect is the same: worldly humiliation is located before the later resurrection-day punishment. By sitting between recipient and disgrace, the preposition delays the subject until the domain has been named.

topics.headline: preposition locates disgrace in the world
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that punishment is already located in the near-life domain before the final-day sentence arrives.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following world noun and frames the nominal disgrace clause.

topics.headline: domain inserted before disgrace noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the sentence assign him and locate the domain before finally naming disgrace.
topics.reason: The preposition phrase sits between the fronted recipient and the delayed subject.

words.gloss_range: the definite nearer and lower life-domain, governed by the locative preposition and contrasted with the later reckoning frame
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, lowness, approach, and the lexicalized nearer life; here the world is the proximate and lower domain of disgrace
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلدُّنْيَا}} ({{tr:al-dunyā}}) names the nearer domain where disgrace is assigned. Its elative shape makes the word feel comparative: this life is near and lower, with a farther counterpart implied even before the ayah names the Day of Rising. Governed by the locative preposition, it is the container of disgrace, and it begins the two-domain sentencing pattern that later surah language develops (22:11).

topics.headline: definite elative names the nearer domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word itself presupposes a nearer-lower life against a farther counterpart.
topics.reason: The local form is a definite lexicalized feminine elative naming the nearer life, not merely a raw comparative adjective.

topics.headline: near and low domain contains disgrace
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels worldly disgrace as both proximate in time and lower in rank.
topics.reason: The prepositional government makes the word the domain of the disgrace, while root pressure preserves nearness and lowness.

topics.headline: worldly frame opens domain contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah’s first punishment domain set before the resurrection-day domain, with the near-life field recurring nearby (22:11).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows connect this word to the later temporal frame and to the nearby loss language in 22:11.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative disgrace or public humiliation as delayed subject, assigned in the nearer life
words.root_gloss_range: disgrace, humiliation, exposure to contempt, shameful loss, and causative disgracing; here the noun names the assigned state rather than the act
words.prose: {{ar:خِزْىٌۭ}} ({{tr:khizyun}}) finally names what has been assigned to him in the nearer life. Its indefiniteness leaves the worldly disgrace open-ended rather than a single known penalty, and as a verbal noun it presents a state lodged with him rather than an active verb of disgracing. The public-exposure sense matches the outward arrogance of the turned side: hidden lack of knowledge becomes visible humiliation. The phrase belongs to a recurrent worldly-disgrace pattern, including parallels with different recipients (11:66; 39:26) and a nearby domain shift in 22:11.

topics.headline: indefinite delayed disgrace
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that recipient and domain are fixed before an open-ended disgrace is named.
topics.reason: The noun is nominative, indefinite, and delayed after fronted predicates in a nominal sentence.

topics.headline: disgrace as visible state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the inward epistemic failure and bodily arrogance answered by outward humiliation.
topics.reason: The root field supports public humiliation, and the surface verbal noun names the state rather than a causative act.

topics.headline: recurrent worldly disgrace pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes this as part of a wider worldly-disgrace formula, re-anchored to this disputer.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite recurrent pairings and concrete parallels (11:66; 22:11; 39:26).

words.root_display: no lexical root (particle or function word)
words.gloss_range: coordinating connector that adds the eschatological punishment clause to the worldly disgrace clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the worldly disgrace sentence to the eschatological tasting sentence, so the two punishments accumulate rather than replace each other. It also moves the ayah from a static nominal state to active divine speech. Its brevity makes the escalation syntactically light, and after the nunated disgrace it gives a small vocal reset before the divine verb enters.

topics.headline: worldly and eschatological clauses coordinated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the next punishment is added to worldly disgrace, not offered as an alternative explanation of it.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the following verbal clause as coordinated with the worldly punishment statement.

topics.headline: connector starts active divine action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the movement from assigned state to divine action at the connector.
topics.reason: The connector stands between a nominal verdict clause and a verbal first-person punishment clause.

topics.headline: brief sound reset before divine verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a small transition before the active divine verb begins.
topics.reason: The sound note is locally tied to the boundary between the disgrace noun and the next verb.

words.gloss_range: first-person plural causative tasting verb with attached object, making the tracked man undergo punishment as direct sensory experience
words.root_gloss_range: tasting, sampling, direct experience, and causative making someone taste; here Form IV selects imposed experiential punishment
words.prose: {{ar:نُذِيقُهُۥ}} ({{tr:nudhīquhu}}) brings divine first-person action into the ayah after third-person description. The object suffix keeps the same man in view, while the indicative form asserts the punishment rather than subordinating it like the earlier misguiding verb. The taste root and Form IV morphology make the punishment imposed sensory experience: he is made to taste it, not merely informed of it. Variant singular divine voice sharpens the register as contrast, and nearby echoes keep the tasting-punishment field active (22:22; 22:25).

topics.headline: divine voice acts on the same target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from describing him to God directly imposing consequence on him.
topics.reason: The verb is first-person plural with a 3ms object suffix, and the suffix tracks the same figure from the previous clauses.

topics.headline: punishment becomes made-to-taste experience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels punishment as compulsory direct experience rather than an abstract sentence.
topics.reason: The Form IV verb and its punishment object license causative sensory-experience language, supported by the dominant tasting-punishment collocation.

topics.headline: variant tightens divine voice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can register a sharper singular-voice contrast while the standard local surface remains first-person plural.
topics.reason: The variant changes voice-register and connector force but preserves the imposed tasting action; it does not replace the aligned surface.

topics.headline: tasting punishment recurs nearby
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this imposed tasting as part of a nearby surah pattern that returns as command and threat.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows link this verb with related tasting-punishment language in 22:22 and 22:25.

words.gloss_range: accusative temporal adverb and construct head, locating the imposed tasting in the Day defined by rising
words.root_gloss_range: day, time, appointed period, epoch, and crisis-time; here the accusative adverb marks the appointed reckoning frame
words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) locates the imposed tasting in time as an accusative adverb, and as construct head it is defined by the following rising-event noun. The word is not a new participant; it opens the final temporal frame. Its day-field can mark an appointed epoch or crisis-time, so the punishment is placed in a bounded reckoning moment rather than merely a calendar day. The familiar formula recurs in the surah’s judgment scenes (22:17; 22:69).

topics.headline: accusative day frames tasting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the tasting is temporally located, while the day is defined by the following event.
topics.reason: The word is an accusative temporal adverb and construct head governing the following genitive noun.

topics.headline: day as appointed crisis-time
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the time as an appointed reckoning frame, not a simple solar-day label.
topics.reason: The broader day/period field survives as temporal pressure while the local construct selects the resurrection-day formula.

topics.headline: formula opens final punishment beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a recognized judgment-time formula beginning the final punishment segment, with surah echoes at 22:17 and 22:69.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows connect the phrase with the yawm-qiyāma formula and concrete surah references.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive rising or standing event that defines the Day of punishment
words.root_gloss_range: standing, rising, establishing, straightening, maintaining, community-standing, and resurrection; here the definite event noun names the eschatological standing-to-account
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ}} ({{tr:al-qiyāmati}}) defines the Day by the act of rising or standing. Its definiteness makes the event identifiable, and its genitive role means the day is named by that standing-event rather than by a neutral date. The root field of standing, establishment, and straightness creates a strong reversal after deviation from the path: the one who turns away from the course is placed in a standing-to-account frame. The communal and formulaic judgment force remains local as eschatological framing, not a command to establish something.

topics.headline: definite event defines the day
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punishment time is defined by rising or standing, not by a neutral date.
topics.reason: The definite genitive event noun completes the temporal construct and is formulaically paired with the day word.

topics.headline: uprightness field answers path deviation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the path-deviation theme answered by a final standing-to-account frame.
topics.reason: The root field supports standing, establishment, and uprightness pressure; local grammar selects the resurrection event, not command forms or all root branches.

topics.headline: individual punishment placed in collective judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the individual disputer’s punishment is set inside the surah’s wider judgment scene.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah row ties this event noun to other judgment scenes in the surah.

words.gloss_range: accusative punishment object made to be tasted, construct-bound to the burning specification
words.root_gloss_range: punishment, torment, chastisement, and a polarity with sweetness or sweet water; here punishment is the tasted content specified as burning
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابَ}} ({{tr:ʿadhāba}}) is the explicit object that the divine verb makes him taste. It also governs the final burning word in construct, so the punishment is both the content of tasting and the head of a burning specification. The noun form lets the verb carry the action while this word carries the content. The root’s sweet-water polarity becomes meaningful because the governing verb is a taste verb: the penalty is a bitter reversal inside a sensory field. The same burning-punishment phrase is announced here and later voiced as direct command (22:22), with wider formula parallels (3:181; 8:50; 85:10).

topics.headline: punishment is what is tasted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices punishment as the content made experiential, not as a separate circumstance after the verb.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the word as the explicit object of the tasting verb and the construct head of the burning genitive.

topics.headline: taste verb activates bitter reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the punishment as a bitter sensory reversal while the local noun still means torment or punishment.
topics.reason: The sweet-water branch is not the local sense, but the taste construction makes the polarity reader-facing.

topics.headline: announced phrase answered later
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this punishment phrase as a specialized formula that returns as direct tasting command in 22:22.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite the constrained formula and concrete echoes (3:181; 8:50; 22:22; 85:10).

words.gloss_range: definite genitive burning or conflagration term specifying the punishment at the ayah close
words.root_gloss_range: burning, burning sensation, fire, conflagration, and scorched severity; here the definite gerund specifies the punishment as burning fire-state
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَرِيقِ}} ({{tr:al-ḥarīqi}}) closes the ayah as the definite genitive that specifies the punishment. The gerund or state-noun form names burning as the punishment’s character, not a command to ignite. Its rare root and punishment-taste clustering make the close severe and specialized, while internal burning-sensation pressure suits the fact that the punishment is tasted. The same close returns later as direct command (22:22), and the boundary reverses the absent illuminating light of 22:8 into imposed burning. The harsh pharyngeal-to-uvular sound frame adds closure texture without carrying the lexical sense by itself.

topics.headline: definite genitive specifies punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word specifies the kind of punishment as a burning state, not a generic pain.
topics.reason: The word is definite, genitive, and governed by the punishment noun as its specification.

topics.headline: rare burn root intensifies tasted punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the punishment as severe and sensory, with external fire and internal burning pressure converging.
topics.reason: The rarity and branch evidence support a specialized burning term, while the tasting construction makes internalized burning pressure relevant.

topics.headline: closing fire answers later and reverses missing light
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the closing burn term anticipate 22:22 and answer the missing illuminating light from 22:8.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows connect this close to 22:22 and to the boundary movement from absent illumination in 22:8 to burning fire in 22:9.

topics.headline: guttural frame closes the ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final word’s constricted sound reinforce the severity of the burning close.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows add local closure texture without changing the specified burning sense.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The thani/atfihi posture at words 1-2 and the causative li-yudilla ... sabil construction at words 3-5.
baseline_models.mechanism: The agent folds his own side away and turns that self-direction into the purposive redirection of others. The body is both a display of refusal and an instrument that bends movement away from the intended way.

activation_trace.role: Folding and turning supply the initiating bodily deflection.
The side bent away makes the gesture one of refusal and proud disengagement.
Departure from intended direction is the effect causatively imposed on others.
A traversable extended way spatializes what the agent diverts people from.

changed_reading.before: A proud person adopts dismissive body language while arguing.
changed_reading.after: His bodily turn is itself a routing act: he advertises a deflection and reproduces it in other travelers.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causative yudilla at word 3 governs movement away from sabil at word 5.
baseline_models.mechanism: The loss root permits more than choosing the wrong road: concealment and loss make the correct route unavailable to perception or recovery. The misleader can therefore operate by obscuring access as well as by recommending an alternative.

activation_trace.role: Concealment supplies a mechanism in which the way disappears from view.
Loss supplies the traveler's inability to locate or recover the way.
The extended road is the object whose visibility and availability are impaired.

changed_reading.before: Misleading means transmitting an incorrect proposition.
changed_reading.after: Misleading can mean making God's traversable way hidden, lost, or practically unrecoverable.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired worldly disgrace and resurrection-day tasting in words 9-15.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah stages consequence in two theaters: public abasement in the near world and first-person sensory verification at the rising event. Tasting converts a future judicial statement into experienced material knowledge.

activation_trace.role: The nearer world supplies the first temporal horizon.
Public abasement and exposure make the first consequence social and visible.
Experiential testing makes the second consequence personally verified.
A day as a severe event marks the decisive second horizon.
Rising and resurrection identify the event in which the second consequence is encountered.
Severe punitive pain gives the tasting its judicial force.
Actual flame gives the future experience a material medium.

changed_reading.before: The verse lists one punishment now and another later.
changed_reading.after: It moves from visible social exposure in the near horizon to direct sensory knowledge of burning at the rising.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding sequence forms a directional relay: a warrantless disputant follows a rebellious source, affiliation makes him the recipient of misguidance, and the focus figure then causatively misguides others. His turned side can thus display an orientation he first received and now transmits.

activation_trace.role: The focus body's turn is the visible hinge through which direction is relayed.
The focus causative action sends others away from the intended direction.
Following behind another supplies the upstream reception of direction.
Opposition and crookedness characterize the source whose line is followed.
Affiliative loyalty makes the directional influence a social attachment.
An earlier causative instance supplies the incoming misguidance in the relay.
Road-leading is inverted toward punishment, exposing the relay's anti-guidance.

structural_cues: 22:3-4 place following, affiliation, misguidance, and inverted guidance immediately before the focus disputant.
22:8 repeats the warrantless-disputation frame immediately before 22:9.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the ordered follow-affiliate-mislead sequence; I infer that 22:9 occupies the next social link. A live alternative is that 22:3-4 and 22:8-9 describe parallel, not serial, types.

changed_reading.before: The focus figure is a self-originating influencer.
changed_reading.after: He is also a relay node who converts received crooked orientation into outgoing causative misguidance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The nearby edge-worshipper is stable only while benefit arrives, then reverses onto his face and reaches far misguidance. That sequence turns the focus flank from a static badge of pride into the outward form of a precarious orientation that can flip and then recruit others into its distance.

activation_trace.role: The focus fold supplies an already unstable bodily angle.
Inclination of the side gives the focus posture its directional bias.
Inclination away from a direction makes edge worship a precarious orientation.
Turning a thing over from its face supplies the trial-triggered reversal.
The face as direction makes the reversal a total reorientation.
The resulting state is explicitly departure from guidance.
Distance measures how far the unstable turn carries its subject.

structural_cues: 22:11 sequences conditional stability, trial, bodily inversion, and loss of both temporal horizons.
22:12 names the endpoint as far misguidance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two adjacent bodily turns and their directional outcomes; I infer that the focus agent externalizes and propagates the instability shown in 22:11. The agents may instead be distinct portraits.

changed_reading.before: Turning the flank is only deliberate arrogance.
changed_reading.after: It is also the social projection of edge-balanced allegiance: a reversible posture that sends others into the same far displacement.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across the surah, bodies circle, stand, bow, and lower themselves toward God. The focus body also bends, but away. The same physical capacity is polarized into worshipful orientation and anti-worshipful deflection, making the turned flank a counter-bow.

activation_trace.role: Bending supplies the bodily motion shared with, but redirected against, worship.
The side turned in refusal distinguishes this bend from submission.
Lowering the head supplies the surah-wide bodily direction of submission.
Circling organizes movement around the purified center rather than away from it.
Upright standing supplies one stable ritual posture at the sanctuary.
Bowing and lowering the head supply the positive counterpart to the focus bend.
Lowering oneself in humility completes the sanctuary's posture sequence.

structural_cues: 22:18 places cosmic and human prostration against the subset for whom punishment is due.
22:26 gathers circling, standing, bowing, and prostrating bodies around the house.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies contrasting bends and their objects; I assign the anti-bow relation between them. A live alternative is that the focus posture is only a social idiom with no ritual contrast.

changed_reading.after: The posture is a counter-ritual use of the body: curvature directed away from the center to which other bodies bow.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later context materializes God's way as guidance to a praised path, access to the sacred mosque, deliberate travel toward a revered destination, and arrivals through mountain passes. The focus misguidance therefore scales from rhetoric to route control: obscuring, diverting, or obstructing embodied access to a shared center.

activation_trace.role: The focus causative verb supplies active diversion from intended direction.
The focus way is already a traversable route rather than a free-floating theme.
Repeated road-leading gives the positive directional process opposed by the focus agent.
Turning others away converts directional error into deliberate obstruction.
The focus route recurs beside the sacred mosque and acquires an access dimension.
Intentional travel toward what is revered gives the route a shared destination.
Open passes between mountains make the approach concrete and geographically plural.

structural_cues: 22:24-27 moves from being guided to a path, through blocking the way and mosque, to travelers arriving from every deep pass.
22:25 makes resident and visitor equal at the shared sanctuary.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies lexical recurrence and an access sequence; I infer that personal misguidance and institutional obstruction are scalable forms of one routing mechanism. The focus agent may remain only a rhetorician.

changed_reading.before: He persuades listeners to adopt a wrong belief.
changed_reading.after: He interferes with a lived route to a shared sanctuary, so misguidance can include social and spatial denial of access.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus forecast is replayed as a loop: sufferers attempt to pass outward, are returned, and are told to taste the same burning punishment; the tasting formula then recurs beside obstruction of God's way. Punishment is not one instant but repeated sensory verification under denied egress.

activation_trace.role: The focus prediction defines punishment as personally tested experience.
Punitive pain gives the experience judicial force.
Flame supplies the material repeatedly encountered.
Attempted passage to the outside introduces an escape trajectory.
Return after departure closes the attempted trajectory into a loop.
The focus mode of experiential testing is explicitly repeated inside the loop.
The same punitive category confirms continuity with the focus forecast.
The same burning medium completes the near-verbatim replay.
Tasting recurs in the verse that names obstruction of God's way.
Punishment directly links the obstruction scene to the focus consequence.

structural_cues: 22:19-22 encloses bodies in material fire and repeats the focus phrase after each attempted exit.
22:25 places another tasting formula in the same sentence as blocking God's way and the sacred mosque.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies recurrence, attempted exit, forced return, and the obstruction-tasting link; I infer a reciprocal blocker-becomes-blocked pattern. A live alternative is simple elaboration without measure-for-measure force.

changed_reading.before: The future clause promises a single later experience of fire.
changed_reading.after: The promised tasting unfolds as a recursive denied-exit experience and echoes back onto the act of denying others a way.

context_deltas.mechanism: Travel through the earth is presented as enabling hearts to reason, while the actual blindness lies in hearts; later guidance terminates in a straight path. A way is therefore an epistemic instrument, not merely a destination. Diverting people from it deprives them of the movement that could correct inner blindness.

activation_trace.role: Concealment lets misguidance operate by keeping corrective orientation unavailable.
The traversable way supplies the medium of corrective movement.
Going and flowing through the earth initiates the context's learning process.
The heart is named both as the organ enabled by travel and as the organ that can remain blind.
Reason as a restraint on ignorance supplies the cognitive result of travel.
Inner blindness identifies the condition that an unblocked journey could expose and correct.
Gentle road-leading supplies the positive epistemic direction.
Straightness and rectitude define the path's corrected orientation.

structural_cues: 22:46 grammatically links traveling in the earth with acquiring hearts that reason and ears that hear.
22:54 links recognized truth, yielding hearts, and guidance to a straight path.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies travel-to-reason and truth-to-straight-guidance sequences; I infer that blocking the path disables a corrective feedback process. A live alternative is that physical travel only furnishes evidence, while the focus way remains doctrinal.

changed_reading.before: God's way is an external route leading to a destination.
changed_reading.after: The way is also a learning process; diverting someone from it can preserve the heart's blindness by preventing corrective travel.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus posture is framed by coiled dispute without guidance or illuminating warrant. Near the surah's end, worship without authoritative proof and visible denial on faces approach bodily assault against reciters. The turned flank can therefore function as coercive body language within an escalation from argument to intimidation.

activation_trace.role: The refusing side gives disputation a visible bodily force.
Causative diversion identifies the social result sought by the display.
Twisted adversarial disputation supplies the immediate speech setting.
Compelling proof is precisely absent, leaving coercion without warrant.
The visible front of the body carries denial before threatened action.

structural_cues: 22:8 supplies the focus person's warrantless-disputation frame.
22:72 moves from recognizable denial on faces to near-assault on those reciting the signs.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated warrantless dispute and a later face-to-assault sequence; I infer an escalation mechanism joining them. The later hostile group need not be the individual of 22:9.

changed_reading.before: The flank turn merely describes the speaker's attitude.
changed_reading.after: It is performative intimidation: a bodily stage in enforcing misdirection when compelling proof is absent.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later transmission scene contains a thrown intrusion, its removal, the securing of signs, and renewed guidance to straightness. This activates an informational reading of the focus: the sideways human posture introduces a perturbation into the communicative route, while correction removes the insertion and restores direction.

activation_trace.role: Inclination supplies the sideways perturbation in the focus scene.
Concealment supplies the informational effect of the perturbation.
Casting an item into a stream supplies the intrusive insertion.
Crooked opposition identifies the insertion's adversarial source.
Removal followed by replacement supplies the first repair operation.
Securing and perfecting supply the stabilization of the signs after removal.
Restored road-leading supplies the repaired transmission's effect.
Straightness marks the recovered direction after correction.

structural_cues: 22:52 orders casting, removal, and securing within one transmission sequence.
22:53-54 contrasts vulnerable hearts with knowledgeable hearts that yield and are guided straight.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an insertion-repair-guidance sequence; I analogize the focus misleader to human-scale interference in a message route. A live alternative is that the later sequence concerns a different mechanism and only shares adversarial direction.

changed_reading.before: The focus agent only redirects people interpersonally.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, he also models informational interference: a sideways insertion that obscures a message until its route is repaired.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the numerical and road-bend branches of thani rather than treating the word only as an idiom of posture. It remains anchored in focus word 1 beside the explicit way at word 5 and is sharpened by later intended, open, and straight routes. Downstream prose should call it an imagistic second-road model, not a grammatical replacement for the ordinary construction.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Thani at word 1 read beside sabil at word 5.

activation_trace.role: Making one into two supplies a duplicate route alongside the first.
A bend in a mountain or valley road gives the duplicate the shape of a detour.
The traversable way is the primary route beside which the detour is imagined.
A clear intended road supplies the legitimate route toward the revered center.
Wide passes between mountains make road branching spatially imaginable.
Straightness distinguishes the authorized orientation from the manufactured detour.

changed_reading.before: A person turns his side while drawing others off one road.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, he manufactures a second, bent road beside the intended one and makes the detour look traversable.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates material cord and trap branches beneath a bodily idiom. It remains anchored in the doubled/turned focus posture and its causative effect, with later cord-cutting and holding-fast language supplying a coherent attachment topology. Downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for manipulated allegiance, not as the lexical sense demanded by 22:9.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The doubled turn at words 1-2 as the mechanism serving causative misguidance at word 3.

activation_trace.role: A cord doubled at its ends supplies a line capable of redirecting what is attached.
A bent trap supplies capture through controlled curvature.
Directional displacement is the effect produced on the captured attachment.
A cord or connection supplies an explicit attachment line elsewhere in the surah.
Severing supplies the destructive alternative to a stable connection.
A fastening held onto supplies the positive counter-image of secure attachment to God.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it works by manipulating attachment: a doubled lead or bent snare reroutes allegiance away from a secure hold.

strongest_changes: The focus figure becomes a relay node who converts received crooked orientation into outgoing causative misguidance.
God's way becomes an embodied and institutional route to the sanctuary, so misguidance includes obstruction of movement and access.
The repeated tasting language turns final fire into recursive denied egress and echoes consequence back onto path obstruction.
Edge worship, reversal, prostration, and straight guidance polarize the flank turn as unstable anti-worship rather than mere attitude.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context repeatedly re-materialized the focus geometry: body angle became pilgrimage routing, heart cognition, message transmission, and an exit-return punishment loop without forcing those mechanisms into one final interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: The relay model depends on reading adjacent disputants as a social chain rather than independent examples.
The sanctuary-access model may scale an individual rhetorician into institutional obstruction more strongly than the focus alone permits.
The second-road and tethered-snare outliers remain productive material analogies but are deliberately branch-distant.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Bodily turning becomes directional sabotage.** `ث ن ي B005` supplies bending and turning aside, `ع ط ف B003` the side turned away in arrogance, `س ب ل B001` a traversed way, and `ض ل ل B001` departure from aim. Posture is followed by the purpose of misdirecting others. I infer that the bodily turn externalizes and transmits an inward refusal. The verse reads the bent flank as an enacted counter-direction to God's way, not as incidental description.
2. **Exposure now, tested burning later.** `خ ز ي B001` is humiliation through exposure and rejection; `ذ و ق B002` is undergoing or testing an experience; `ح ر ق B002/B003` is flame and burning hurt. The worldly and resurrection consequences are temporally paired. I infer that public disgrace exposes the posture while later burning makes its consequence bodily knowable. “Taste” therefore marks punishment as direct experiential verification of what the disputant denied.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 22:31 magnified the posture into a full spatial catastrophe: divided allegiance turns a sideward refusal into falling, snatching, and wind-driven remoteness.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A bodily fold becomes social diversion.** Fixed `ثَانِى` activates `ث ن ي:B005` (folding, bending, and turning aside), `عِطْفِه` activates `ع ط ف:B003` (turning the flank away in aversion), and `سَبِيل` activates `س ب ل:B001` (extended traversed way). The posture follows argument in `22:8` and receives its consequence through the hands in `22:10`. The packet supplies posture, purpose, and path; I infer that embodied aversion recruits others into the same deviation. The ayah reads the bent side as an enacted politics of misdirection, not a private gesture.
2. **Humiliation exposes what proud posture tried to stage.** Fixed `خِزْى` uses `خ ز ي:B001` (humiliation through exposure and rejection), while `ذ و ق:B002` makes punishment an experienced test. The elevated posture is answered first in the nearer domain (`د ن و:B002`, the nearer/lower side) and then on the event-day (`ي و م:B003`). I infer a reversal from performed elevation to public exposure. The two outcomes read as one disclosure across temporal domains.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later `22:10` relocates the fixed posture into the agent's own hands. That shift corrected any purely theatrical reading: the bent side is conduct sent ahead and returned as consequence.

baseline.text: Allah'ın yolundan saptırmak için böbürlenerek yan çevirir. Ona dünyada rezillik vardır; kıyamet günü ona yakıcı ateşin azabını tattırırız.

findings.text: Bedenin kibirle yana dönmesi, başkalarını da Allah'ın yolundan saptıran toplumsal bir karşı yönelişe dönüşür.
Dünyadaki aşağılanma, sergilenen üstünlük duruşunu açığa çıkarır; sonraki yakıcı azap ise sonucunu doğrudan yaşatır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, iki sayısını ve iki öğeli birliği temel alır; bir şeyi ikiye çıkarma, bir başkasına ikinci olma ve ilk işe ikinci bir iş ekleme kullanımlarını açıkça aynı dalda toplar. Doğumla ilgili anlatım da bu ikilik çekirdeğine bağlıdır, ancak iki çocuk doğurma ile ikinci doğumu yapma yorumları birlikte korunmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal sayı ve ikilik çekirdeğiyle sınırlıdır; yineleme, katlama, övgü ve dışarıda bırakma anlamları buraya katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, sayı ve türemiş biçimlerdeki ikilik çekirdeğini kapsar; ikişerli dağılım ve belirli söz öbekleri yalnız kendi yapıları içinde ele alınır.

concept_map.definition: İki sayısını bildirme, bir varlığa bir başkasını katarak toplamı ikiye çıkarma ya da iki kişiden biri olarak ikinci konumda bulunma anlam alanıdır. İkişerli dağılım ile iki çocuk veya ikinci çocuk doğurma, bu çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: İki sayısını ve birlikte bulunan iki öğeden oluşan birliği bildirir.
Bir öğeye ikincisini katıp bütünü ikiye çıkarır veya bir başkasına ikinci kişi olur.
Bir topluluğun ikişer ikişer düzenlenmesini ya da hareket etmesini anlatır.
Doğum kullanımında iki çocuk doğurma ile ikinci çocuğu doğurma yorumları yan yana bulunur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar iki sayısı, bir şeyi iki yapma, bir başkasının yanında ikinci olma ve ilk öğeye ikinci bir öğe ekleme çekirdeğinde birleşir. İkişerli dağılımı da bu alana bağlar; doğum örneğinde ise iki çocuk ile ikinci çocuk yorumlarının ikisi de aktarılır.

concept_gloss.text: iki olma, ikiye çıkarma veya ikili oluşturma
concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın sayı, ekleme, ikinci olma, ikişerli düzen ve doğumla ilgili ikilik çekirdeğinin tamamını temsil eder.

error_profile.preserves: İki sayısını, ikiye çıkarma işlemini ve ikili birliğin bütün temel gerçekleşmelerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şeye ikinci bir öğe katma veya onu iki öğeli duruma getirme bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bir öğeyi ekleme yoluyla ikiye çıkarma işlemini doğal biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: Sayı adı, ikinci kişi olma, ikişerli dağılım ve doğum kullanımlarını göstermez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişilerin veya nesnelerin ikili kümeler halinde dağıldığı ya da ilerlediği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İkili kümeler halinde dağılım ve ilerleme anlamını eksiksiz korur.
error_profile.loses: İkiye çıkarma, ikinci kişi olma ve doğumla ilgili kullanımları kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Doğum kullanımının ikinci doğumu öne çıkaran yorumunda doğal karşılık olarak kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Doğum kullanımındaki ikinci çocuk yorumunu açık biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: İki çocuk doğurma yorumunu ve dalın sayı ile ekleme çekirdeğini dışarıda bırakır.

branches.branch_image_ar: ضم واحد إلى واحد وجعلهما اثنين
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الاثنان والاثنتان وثاني اثنين ومثنى مثنى، وتثنية الشيء بجعله اثنين أو صيرورة المرء ثانيا لغيره أو ضم شيء ثان إلى الأول، ومنه ولادة الثاني أو الاثنين.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه المدح المسمى ثناء، ولا الاستثناء، ولا طي الشيء وثنيه حسيا.
branches.source_phrase_ar: الاثنان في العدد معروفان؛ امرأة ثنى ولدت اثنين (maqayis)؛ ثنيته تثنية أي جعلته اثنين؛ اثنان من عدد المذكر واثنتان للمؤنث؛ هذا ثاني اثنين أي أحد الاثنين (sihah)؛ فلان ثاني اثنين أي هو أحدهما؛ وإذا فعل الرجل أمرا ثم ضم إليه أمرا آخر قيل ثنى بالأمر الثاني (tahdhib)؛ الثني والاثنان أصل لمتصرفات هذه الكلمة؛ كنت له ثانيا أو ضممت إليه ما صار به اثنين (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, önderden sonra gelen ve üstünlük sıralamasında birinci olamayan kişiyi açıkça tanımlar. Aile içindeki düşük konum anlatımı da genel bir ikinci sıra adı değil, bu aşağı derecenin kalıplaşmış ve daha sert bir uzantısıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal sayısal ikiden çok toplumsal sıra ve üstünlük derecesine bağlıdır; herhangi bir ikinci sırayı kendiliğinden kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, önderin ardından gelen kişi biçimini temel alır; aile içindeki düşük konum yalnız verilen söz öbeğine bağlı bir uzantıdır.

concept_map.definition: Önderin veya en üstün kişinin ardından gelen, saygınlık sıralamasında ona göre daha aşağıda bulunan kişiyi anlatır. Aile içindeki kalıplaşmış kullanım, bu sıra ilişkisini en düşük veya değersiz konuma kadar sertleştirir.

facets.statement: Önderden sonra gelen ve üstünlük sıralamasında ikinci yerde bulunan kişiyi belirtir.
Aile içindeki kullanımda kişinin düşük, yetersiz veya en değersiz konumda olduğunu sezdirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, önderden sonra gelen ve üstünlükte ilk sıraya çıkamayan kişi üzerinde birleşir. Aileyle kurulan söz öbeği bu sıra anlamını düşük konum ve değersizlik imasına genişletir.

concept_gloss.text: önderden sonra gelen veya alt sıradaki kişi
concept_gloss.applicability: Üstünlük sırasındaki ikinci kişiyi ve kalıplaşmış aile kullanımındaki düşük konum uzantısını birlikte karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Önderle kurulan sıra ilişkisini ve bu ilişkinin aşağı konum uzantısını birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir topluluğun saygınlık sıralamasında önderden sonra gelen kişi söz konusu olduğunda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Önderden sonra gelme ve ikinci sırada bulunma ilişkisini korur.
error_profile.loses: Aile içindeki en düşük konumu bildiren sertleşmiş kullanımı göstermez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Aile içindeki saygınlık eksikliğini ve aşağı konumu belirten kalıplaşmış anlatımda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Aile içindeki düşük konum ve değersizlik imasını açıkça korur.
error_profile.loses: Önderin ardından gelen ikinci kişi biçimindeki genel sıra çekirdeğini kapsamaz.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: önderin ardından gelen, ondan aşağı sıradaki kişi

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal toplumsal üstünlük ve saygınlık sırasıdır; komşu dal ise yarış içindeki izleme konumudur.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da üst konumdaki kişiden sonra gelen biri vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalda aşağı sıra belirleyicidir; komşu dalda ise ardından gelmenin yanında görevi devralma işlevi bulunur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Düşüklüğü önderin ardından gelme biçimindeki belirli bir sıra ilişkisine bağlar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: İkinci sıra koşulu olmadan genel olarak aşağı tabakayı, bayağılığı ve değersizliği kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: ikinci sıradaki ile genel olarak aşağı

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın düşük konumu bir üstünlük sıralamasından doğar; komşu dal doğrudan genel düşüklüğü adlandırır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; seçilenler ikinci sıra, yerine geçme ve genel düşüklük arasındaki gerçek karışma noktalarını gösterir, kalanlar yalnız makam alanını paylaşır.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الثنى والثنيان والثني بمعنى الذي يجيء بعد السيد أو دون الأول في السؤدد، ويشمل التعبير عن دنو المنزلة مثل ثنية أهل بيته.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه مطلق العدد اثنين، ولا تكرار الفعل مرتين، ولا السن المسماة ثنية.
branches.source_phrase_ar: الثنى والثنيان الذي يكون بعد السيد كأنه ثانية (maqayis)؛ الثنيان بالضم الذي يكون دون السيد في المرتبة؛ فلان ثنية أهل بيته أي أرذلهم (sihah)؛ الذي يجيء ثانيا في السؤدد ولا يجيء أولا ثنى وثنيان وثني (tahdhib)؛ الثنيان الذي يثنى به إذا عد السادات؛ فلان ثنية أهل بيته كناية عن قصور منزلته (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, bir işin iki kez veya birbiri ardından yeniden yapılmasını dalın açık çekirdeği olarak verir. Aynı yıl içinde bir ödemenin ikinci kez alınmaması ile pay veya iyiliğin yeniden verilmesi örnekleri bu çekirdeğin koşullu gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal salt iki sayısını değil, aynı işin ikinci gerçekleşmesini veya art arda yinelenmesini gerektirir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel yineleme çekirdeği korunur; ödeme, pay ve iyilikle kurulan söz öbeklerinin özel yorumları tüm dala yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir işi ikinci kez yapmak veya aynı şeyi birbiri ardından yeniden gerçekleştirmek anlamıdır. İkinci kez ödeme alma yasağı ile payı ya da iyiliği tekrar verme ve alma kullanımları bu yineleme çekirdeğine bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Aynı işin iki kez veya birbiri ardından yeniden yapılmasını bildirir.
Belirli bir yıl içinde aynı ödemenin ikinci kez alınmasını reddeden kullanımda görülür.
Bir payı yeniden almak veya yapılan iyiliği ikinci ve sonraki kez yinelemek için kullanılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar iki kez yapma ve bir işi yeniden gerçekleştirme çekirdeğinde birleşir. Aynı yıl içinde ikinci kez ödeme alınmaması ortak örnektir; pay alma ve iyilik yapma anlatımları da art arda gerçekleşmeyi gösterir.

concept_gloss.text: bir şeyi ikinci kez ya da art arda yineleme

error_profile.loses: İkiden fazla sürebilen art arda yinelemeyi ve özel ödeme ile pay bağlamlarını kapsamaz.

error_profile.loses: Genel iki kez yapma, ödeme yasağı ve payı yeniden alma anlamlarını kapsamaz.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الثنى بمعنى الأمر المعاد مرتين، وتكرار الأخذ أو اللوم أو المعروف، وما صيغ على مثنى للدلالة على مرة بعد مرة.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه مجرد العدد اثنين بلا إعادة، ولا الاستثناء بوصفه إخراجا من حكم، ولا المثاني إذا أريد بها اسم مخصوص للقرآن أو السور.
branches.source_phrase_ar: الثنى الأمر يعاد مرتين؛ لا ثنى في الصدقة يعني لا تؤخذ في السنة مرتين (maqayis)؛ الثني مقصور الأمر يعاد مرتين؛ لا ثني في الصدقة أي لا تؤخذ في السنة مرتين؛ مثنى الأيادي أن يأخذ القسم مرة بعد مرة (sihah)؛ الثنى إعادة الشيء مرة بعد مرة؛ مثنى الأيادي أن يعيد معروفه مرتين أو ثلاثا (tahdhib)؛ الثنى ما يعاد مرتين؛ لا ثنى في الصدقة أي لا تؤخذ في السنة مرتين (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, okunup yinelenen kitap parçası açıklamasını ve Kur'an'a verilen adı destekler; ancak adın kapsamı kaynaklarda aynı değildir. Bütün metin, açılış bölümü ve iki yüz birimden kısa bölümler ayrı yorumlar olarak korunmalı, tek bir bölüm türü dalın değişmez karşılığı sayılmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yinelenen okuma gerekçesine bağlı kutsal metin adıdır; hangi bölüm veya bütün için kullanıldığı kaynak yorumuna göre değişir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın biçimin metin adı olarak tanıklanan kapsamlarını içerir; genel gündelik yineleme veya başka söz öbekleri bu dala taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Okunup yinelenen bir kitap parçasını, özellikle Kur'an'ın tamamını, açılış bölümünü veya iki yüz birimden kısa bölümlerini adlandıran kullanımdır. Ortak gerekçe yinelenen okumadır, fakat adın kapsadığı metin bölümü kaynak yorumuna göre değişir.

facets.statement: Okunan ve zaman içinde yeniden okunan kitap parçasını yinelenme özelliğiyle adlandırır.
Ad, bir yoruma göre Kur'an'ın tamamını, başka yorumlara göre açılış bölümünü veya daha kısa bölümleri kapsar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar adlandırmayı metnin yeniden okunmasına bağlar. Bununla birlikte kapsamı bütün Kur'an, açılış bölümü ve iki yüz birimden kısa bölümler arasında değiştirir; bu seçenekler tek bir değişmez sınıf gibi birleştirilemez.

concept_gloss.text: tekrar okunan Kur'an bütünü ya da bölümleri
concept_gloss.applicability: Yinelenen okuma gerekçesini ve adın bütün metinden belirli bölüm kümelerine değişen kapsamını birlikte gösterir.

error_profile.preserves: Yinelenen okumayı ve bütün metin, açılış bölümü ile kısa bölümler arasındaki kapsam değişmesini korur.
